issues.description: Check name, CheckID, metadata, and PR semantics disagree on single vs multiple NICs and on PASS/MANUAL/FAIL.
issues.detail: PR title says 'multiple network interfaces' but the directory, CheckID, and CHANGELOG say 'single_network_interface'. Docstring lists MANUAL while metadata only documents PASS/FAIL. Pick one identity for the concept and make code, metadata, changelog, and description all match so future readers can state the invariant without running the code.

issues.description: GKE detection via instance.name.startswith('gke-') is a fragile string-prefix heuristic complecting naming with managed-by identity.
issues.detail: User-controlled names can spoof or miss GKE membership, defeating the MANUAL carve-out. Detect GKE-managed nodes from authoritative signals (goog-gke-node label, kube-env metadata) at the service layer and expose a boolean on Instance. Keep the check a pure count over values; do not smuggle policy into name-sniffing.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch silently emits PASS, hiding an impossible or buggy API shape.
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0 the status remains PASS while status_extended reports 'no network interfaces.' GCE instances always have at least one NIC, so this either masks a bug or papers over an unexpected response with a green check. Either remove the branch or make it explicit MANUAL/INFO with a real reason.

issues.description: Network virtual appliance exemption is documented in metadata Notes but not implemented in code.
issues.detail: Metadata and PR description both call out NVAs as legitimate multi-NIC users, but the code only exempts GKE. The Instance model already exposes ip_forward, the standard NVA signal. Either drop the claim from Notes or route ip_forward instances to MANUAL too; right now the documentation lies about what the check does.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model truncates network/subnetwork self-links and discards accessConfigs/natIP.
issues.detail: Splitting on '/' collapses fully-qualified resource paths into bare names, making two networks named 'default' in different projects indistinguishable. The model also throws away access configs already parsed upstream, forcing future checks to re-walk the API. Preserve full self-links and richer NIC data; derive short labels at display time.

issues.description: Tests do not exercise the MANUAL (GKE) branch or the zero-interface branch.
issues.detail: Coverage hits 1-NIC PASS, 2-NIC FAIL, 3-NIC FAIL, and mixed cases, but the most contested branches (GKE MANUAL and empty interfaces) have no evidence of correctness. Close the truth table with explicit tests for both, so the semantics under dispute are pinned down by examples rather than left to inference.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check addresses a reasonable security concern but ships with mismatched identity across name, CheckID, metadata, changelog, and docstring (single vs multiple, PASS/FAIL vs PASS/MANUAL/FAIL). GKE exemption is detected by fragile name-prefix sniffing instead of authoritative labels/metadata, and the zero-NIC branch silently passes. The documented NVA exemption is not implemented. Service-layer model choices discard identity (truncated self-links) and useful data (accessConfigs). Align naming everywhere, push GKE-ness and NVA-ness onto Instance as first-class fields, decide the zero case deliberately, and close the test truth table before landing.
